title: Capacity hedge derivative scenarios and oncall slab mapping (Apr 2026)
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet maps a small set of derivative-style scenarios that tie short-term price movements (per-token and slab surcharges) to immediate headcount/oncall adjustments and committed capacity reserves. Use this when we need a fast, defensible tradeoff map for sales and ops during a price shock or model-cost surge. Not a final policy — prototype for Q2 playbook.

High-level approach (one pager):
- Define three price-shock axes: transient spike (>48h), sustained uplift (2–12 weeks), and structural shift (>12 weeks).
- For each axis, define a continuum of severity (mild/medium/severe) and compute marginal unit-cost delta per token and per-route.
- Convert cost delta into short-term SLA/coverage obligations and determine the minimum oncall/contractor headcount to maintain target latency SLOs given capacity options (spot vs reserved vs partner-burst).
- Calculate breakeven for the funding lever (temporary surcharge, credit drawdown, or partial rollback of discounts).
- Produce trigger rules: metric thresholds, decision owner, and safe-fallback (model routing to cheaper variant).

Assumptions and knobs (editable cells):
- Baseline token cost (avg across fleet): $0.0009 per token (baseline-mar2026).
- Reserved capacity hourly blended cost: $1.80 / GPU-hour.
- On-demand (spot) blended hourly cost: $0.95 / GPU-hour.
- Average tokens per request: 620 (includes prompt + expected generation).
- Target p50 latency SLO: 150ms per token.
- Engineer oncall capacity: 1 engineer can triage and scale a single lane of burst capacity up to 12 GPU-hours/day with runbook.
- Contractor burst engineer: 0.6x effectiveness versus full-time.

Tabs overview (sheet layout):
Tab: Scenario Matrix (rows)
Columns: scenario_id | axis | severity | delta $/token | delta $/hour GPU | extra GPU-hrs/day needed | oncall FTEs req | contractor days | immediate cash impact/day | 30-day cash impact | suggested pricing dial
Sample rows:
SC-01 | transient_spike | mild | 0.00015 | 0.2 | 24 | 0.5 | 4 | $3,744 | $112,320 | surcharge 5% on new users
SC-02 | transient_spike | severe | 0.0009 | 1.2 | 120 | 2.5 | 20 | $18,720 | $561,600 | temporary surcharge 20% + restrict burst
SC-11 | sustained_uplift | medium | 0.00045 | 0.6 | 60 | 1.2 | 10 | $9,360 | $280,800 | soften discounts for top 10% by volume

Tab: Headcount Bridge
Columns: role | current FTE | ramp lead time (weeks) | marginal cost / month | oncall burden multiplier | trigger rule | contingency pool assignment
Example:
SRE (inference) | 22 | 6 | $18,500 | 1.0 | add 2 FTE at sustained uplift medium | contingency: reserve hire bucket A
Contractor burst SRE | 0 | 1 | $9,500 | 0.6 | used for transient spike severe | contingency: contractor pool C
Cost bridge formula (cells):
- incremental_monthly_labor = sum(added_FTEs * marginal_cost_month)
- daily_capacity_cost = extra_GPU_hrs_per_day * blended_hourly_gpu_cost
- immediate_cash_impact/day = daily_capacity_cost + incremental_daily_labor_pro_ra
- 30-day impact = immediate_cash_impact/day * 30 (adjusted for hire ramp where applicable)

Tab: Pricing Response Ladder
Purpose: quick menu of pricing levers to deploy in order of preference by scenario severity.
Columns: lever | practical_time_to_execute | estimated_revenue_recapture | customer_impact_notes | rollback_condition
Examples:
- reprice-new-accounts (5m API flag) | minutes | low-medium | minimal customer support friction | rollback: 7-day trending improvement
- temporary-surcharge-by-route | 1–2 hours | medium | requires billing notification | rollback: token-price down 20%
- reduce-discount-eligibility | 2–3 days | medium-high | negative sales lift risk | rollback: commit to new credits

Trigger rules (operational snippet):
- If blended token cost spike >= 30% for > 48 hours (transient severe), then auto-enable SC-02 response: engage contractor pool C, enable surcharge flag for new signups, and open SR with capacity-ops to limit burst to reserved-only lanes. Decision owner: Head of Finance (Samantha Park) + Head of Ops for execution.
- If blended token cost delta between 15–30% sustained across 7 days, start headcount bridge hiring (1 FTE SRE inference per 60 GPU-hours/day extra projected) and adjust discounting for top-tier customers with sales sign-off.

Risks and caveats:
- Behavioral: applying surcharges risks churn among high-volume customers; document recommended comms and opt-in credits for strategic partners.
- Measurement: token cost signal can be noisy — use 3-sigma smoothing over 24h to avoid flip-flopping.
- Operational: contractor onboarding time varies; keep warm bench of 8 contractor-days across months for EC2-type events.

Next steps / action items (short):
- Validate blended-cost inputs with infra-finance (Action: Jonas Meyer, due 2026-03-29).
- Wire gsheet formulas into central forecasting model (Action: Elena Kaur, due 2026-04-09).
- Draft customer comms playbook for surcharge and rollback (Action: Ravi Patel + Customer Success, due 2026-04-12).
- Run tabletop simulation for SC-02 with oncall rotation and contractor activation (Action: SRE lead + Finance, scheduled 2026-04-16).

Notes-to-self (working):
- Consider adding an ‘elasticity anchor’: historical take-rate change per 5% surcharge from the 2025 pilot.
- Add column: legal signoff required? for >15% surcharge.
- Keep this sheet as short-term emergency-runbook not a permanent pricing policy.

Revision history:
- 2026-03-22: initial sketch (Samantha Park)
- 2026-03-29: added sample rows and calibrated labor numbers (Jonas)
- 2026-04-05: adjusted blended GPU-hour numbers after infra call (Elena)

End of document.
